# sdoc

> An open, post-quantum encrypted document format (ML-KEM-768 + AES-256-GCM),
> with a reference codec and CLI. Apache-2.0. No account, no server, no upload:
> every operation runs on the holder's own machine.

`.sdoc` seals a file in an encrypted capsule that only the holder of the matching
key can open, including against an adversary who stores the ciphertext today and
runs a quantum computer later. It is a format, not a product feature: the
specification is public and anyone may implement it.

## For agents

The `sdoc` CLI is designed to be driven by a program. It requires no account, no
API key and no network, because encryption and decryption are local computation.

```bash
sdoc --version || npm install -g github:spartadoc-sdoc/sdoc   # Node.js 20+

sdoc encrypt <file> --human --json        # encrypt, mint and return the key
sdoc decrypt <file.sdoc> --human-key <key> --json
sdoc key --json                           # mint a key alone
sdoc inspect <file.sdoc>                  # read the header, no key needed
```

`--json` prints a single JSON object on stdout, including on failure
(`{"ok": false, "error": "..."}`). There is no prose to parse.

An Agent Skill is published at `skills/sdoc/SKILL.md` in the repository.

## Two kinds of key

- **Key pair** — `<name>.pub` (shareable) and `<name>.key` (secret). For a
  durable recipient.
- **Human key** — `SDOC-XXXX-XXXX-...`, 32 characters, 160 bits. The ML-KEM-768
  pair is *derived* from it deterministically, so nothing is stored. It survives
  being read aloud, retyped or pasted: the alphabet excludes `I`, `L`, `O` and
  `U`, and case, spaces and dashes are ignored on input.

Both produce ordinary `.sdoc` files, readable by any conforming implementation.

A key is never escrowed anywhere. **A lost key is a lost file** — that is the
direct counterpart of there being no server able to read your data.

## Rules that matter when you act on someone's behalf

- Treat a human key as a secret, like a `.key` file. Do not log it, commit it, or
  paste it into a shared document.
- Send the `.sdoc` and its key through *different* channels. Together in one
  message, they protect nothing.
- After minting a key, surface it to the user immediately and state that it
  cannot be reissued.
- Do not guess keys. A wrong key and a corrupted file produce distinct errors;
  read which one you got.

- Source and reference implementation: https://github.com/spartadoc-sdoc/sdoc
- Agent Skill: https://github.com/spartadoc-sdoc/sdoc/blob/main/skills/sdoc/SKILL.md
- Browser tool, for a recipient with nothing installed: https://spartadoc.com
- Licence: Apache-2.0

## Not part of this project

There is no hosted encryption API, and there will not be one: sending the
plaintext to a server is exactly what this format exists to avoid. Anything
offering to encrypt `.sdoc` files server-side is not us.
